messages:
kevin: heads-up: after enabling AWQ int8 weight-only with group_size=128 on canary we saw a nasty p95 regression for short-chat workloads (~10-15%). profile attached (see bench-bot logs below). suspect pack/unpack + kernel dispatch overhead + KV cache writebacks are the culprits. anyone seen this pattern before?

maria: ugh. saw something similar with group_size=256 a while back. packing reduced memory but added a copy path that kills tiny seq lengths. do you have seq_len distribution for the canary traffic?

kevin: seq_len median 14, 90th 28. bench-bot output: ```
BENCH RUN: canary-2028-03-15
model: redwood-v1-open
quant: AWQ int8 weight-only, group=128
p95 latency: baseline (fp16+pack-disabled) = 78ms, canary = 90ms (+15%)
CPU copy time (pack/unpack): 9.4ms per request
KV-cache writes increased by ~2.3x (observed via alloc counters)
Kernel switch count (dispatches per token): +18%
```

liz: hmm that copy time is huge relative to 78ms. are we doing background async unpack or blocking on the request thread? if unpack is synchronous we should try offloading to worker pool or use in-place kernel that supports packed layout.

samir: also check calibration: if per-group scales cause the runtime to detect 'poor calibration' we might be falling back to slower kernels for certain layers. any logs showing fallback events?

bench-bot: ```
TRACE: 0x7fa3 kernel_dispatch: selected awq_int8_packed_kernel_v2 for layers [0..22]
TRACE: 0x7fa3 kernel_dispatch: selected fallback_fp32_kernel for layers [23..24] (score drop)
METRIC: kv_cache_writes: baseline=1.0 canary=2.38
METRIC: pack_cpu_us: avg=9400
ALLOC: tmp_buffers_peak_mb: baseline=34 canary=78
```

alex: that fallback for some layers is interesting — could be numeric instability for attn output scales. calibration routine is per-group; if group_size=128 the quant error might spike on narrow layers. try group_size=64 or run an extra per-layer calib pass with outlier clipping.

maria: I ran a quick micro-benchmark on prod-like hw: 
```
# repro (simple loop):
./run_infer --model redwood-v1-open --quant awq --group 128 --seq 16 --batch 1
# observe pack/unpack accounting
```
Results: group=128 p95=93ms, group=64 p95=81ms, fp16 p95=77ms. So group=64 gets us close to baseline. Packing overhead drops ~4.2ms when group smaller (probably smaller buffer sizes -> fewer tmp allocations).

kevin: good data. but group=64 increases model size ~+6% and might affect memory-limited Dedicated nodes. need to weigh throughput/cost. Also KV behavior: packing invalidates our zero-copy KV cache path because packed KV isn't memory-aligned for the fast path; we end up memcpy-ing per request. That explains the kv_cache_writes metric bump.

liz: short-term mitigation: change batching heuristic to prefer non-packed kernel for avg_seq < 32 and batch_size <= 4. That avoids pack/unpack for the common small chats. Long-term: support packed-aligned KV cache layout in runtime or add an in-place pack kernel.

samir: agree. also add a calibration sanity check that refuses a quant config if fallback layers > 10% — better to pick different group_size at model onboarding. we can run an automatic sweep (64/96/128) and store perf+quality profiles in model catalog.

alex: one caution: switching heuristics could change unit costs for high-throughput feeders (long seqs). need canary split and cost tracking.

deploy-bot: canary rollout: canary-2028-03-15 currently at 3% traf split. Proposed change: rollback AWQ group=128 -> group=64 for canary traffic where avg_seq < 32; create canary2 with new batching heuristic at 1% before wider rollout.

kevin: plan: 1) revert canary to group=64 for now (reduce p95), 2) add batching heuristic that disables pack for small seqs (config flag: runtime.pack_threshold_seq=32), 3) schedule an automated group_size sweep during model onboarding and attach calib+perf badge to catalog. I'll open the perf-ops issue.

maria: I'll run the sweep on the staging cluster and attach the per-layer fallback logs + accuracy drift numbers. should have plots by EOD.

liz: i'll sketch the heuristic change and a minimal test in the runtime unit tests. also add a small integration test ensuring packed KV triggers the memcpy path so we don't regress silently.

samir: i'll add a regression alert tied to p95 and kv_cache_writes spikes so we catch any future packs that cause similar regressions.

kevin: thanks all. filing follow-ups: PERF-1248 (rollback + heuristic), PERF-1249 (group sweep + catalog badges), OPS-558 (packed-kv alignment work). cc @maria @liz

bench-bot: log saved to s3://bench-archive/canary/1781234567/pack-profile.log

kevin: closing loop: we'll pause the wider AWQ group=128 rollout until the sweep completes and the heuristic is in canary. :thumbsup:
